subject: Re: Rights allocation & feedback escrow — order form redlines
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightlinehealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@brightlinehealth.com, legal@brightlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial redlines — MSA + Order Form (IP allocation & feedback license)

Hannah / Ben —

Thanks for sending the MSA and updated order form. Our legal team reviewed and marked several redlines focused on IP and productization paths. High level: Brightline needs explicit assignment (or exclusive license) for generated outputs used in our product features, and a carveout not to have those outputs used to train general models that could be re-used outside our tenancy. We appreciate Redwood's platform capabilities but need certainty (and evidence) about telemetry/usage data that might leak training signals.

Key asks from our side:
- Order Form to state "Customer owns or has exclusive rights to output generated by Customer prompts where outputs are used to create or train Customer product features."
- Training prohibition: Redwood not to use Customer prompts/outputs for improving third-party models without opt-in.
- Feedback license: if Brightline shares bug reports or labeled data as feedback, we grant Redwood a limited license solely to improve the Redwood service for Brightline (not for commercial models).
- Escrow / evidence: we may request logs/evidence of deletion/retention and a short-term escrow arrangement for feedback artifacts while integrations are being validated.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept narrow carveouts like the ones above and propose alternate language if needed? Also please point to the page in your docs that defines "telemetry" and "anonymization" practices.

Attached: our redline (Brightline_MSA_redline_20280127.pdf) and a suggested markup to the order form (OrderForm_Brightline_v3.docx).

Best,
Sara Patel
Senior Counsel, Brightline Health

From: hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: sara.patel@brightlinehealth.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jan 2028 10:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — MSA + Order Form (IP allocation & feedback license)

Sara —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Laura (product/ops) to validate implementation and suggested language. Ben — marking for commercial point-of-view (credits / procurement cadence).

Quick replies to your bullets:
- We typically grant customers rights to outputs (customer-owned outputs for product usage) but our core concern is ensuring we can still operate the service (safety telemetry, bug fixes) without retaining material that makes customers identifiable.
- We can accept an opt-out from model-training for Customer-provided prompts/outputs; the practical path is to surface a training_opt_out flag at account level and capture that in the order form. Need to confirm how that affects model quality and support SLAs.
- Feedback license: we have standard language that limits feedback use to service improvements, but Brightline's proposed restriction ("not for commercial models") is stricter than our current baseline. Karthik, any immediate thoughts on a constrained license?
- Escrow for feedback artifacts is unusual but doable as a time-boxed staging/validation step. Laura -- what does this mean operationally (retention, encryption, access controls)?

We will propose redline language for the order form by EOD tomorrow and include a short implementation note on what the training opt-out entails (latency on opt-out, tracing, telemetry retention window).

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sara.patel@brightlinehealth.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jan 2028 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — MSA + Order Form (IP allocation & feedback license)

Sara / team —

From a commercial perspective, Brightline's asks are reasonable but do have price and SLA implications. A training opt-out typically increases per-token cost because we disable certain caching/aggregation paths and need stronger isolation for evaluation. Proposed commercial levers:
- Training opt-out as an add-on at order form level (line item), or included at committed tiers above X spend.
- Short-term escrow / secure staging for feedback artifacts covered as a professional services item (one-time fee).
- We can offer a small onboarding credit to offset one-time engineering work to wire the opt-out flag into Brightline's environment.

Sara, if you can confirm the desired opt-out scope (account-wide vs per-route), I will include an indicative price in the next doc iteration.

— Ben
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sara.patel@brightlinehealth.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 31 Jan 2028 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Draft language — Order Form / MSA (training opt-out & feedback license)

Team / Sara —

Attached below is suggested contract language that balances Brightline's productization needs with Redwood's operational requirements. Happy to iterate but this is intended to be narrow and practical.

1) Order Form clause (training opt-out):
"Customer may elect, by checking the 'Training Opt-Out' box on the Order Form, to prohibit Redwood Inference from using Customer prompts, outputs, or derivative artifacts to train, fine-tune or otherwise improve models that are made generally available outside of Customer's dedicated environment. Such opt-out applies account-wide and will take effect within thirty (30) days of execution. Redwood will continue to collect minimal telemetry necessary for safety and service operation; such telemetry will be retained for no longer than ninety (90) days and shall be stored in aggregated or de-identified form except where explicit customer debugging access is requested."

2) Feedback license (limited):
"To the extent Customer provides Feedback (including labeled examples, bug reports, or other contributed data), Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use such Feedback solely to operate, maintain and improve the Redwood service for Customer, provided that Redwood shall not use Feedback to train or commercialize general-purpose models that are distributed outside Customer's tenancy without Customer's prior written consent. Feedback may be retained in escrow for thirty (30) days during onboarding validations upon mutual agreement reflected in the Order Form."

Notes: these limits preserve Redwood's ability to fix safety/availability issues while giving Brightline strong controls. If Brightline requires an immediate prohibition on any telemetry collection, we will need to evaluate the impact on SLA and error diagnosis.

If Sara/Legal are comfortable with the wording, I can create a tracked-change version of the MSA + order form for signature.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Draft language — Order Form / MSA (training opt-out & feedback license)

Karthik / team —

Operational clarifications before we sign:
- "Take effect within thirty (30) days" is fine, but we should add a line about "no retroactive removal of models or caches" to be explicit about existing KV cache states; opt-out will prevent future aggregated training only.
- 90-day telemetry retention is acceptable if we ensure strong access controls and a documented deletion workflow. I'll prepare the runbook excerpt and export paths.
- Escrow retention window of 30 days is fine for onboarding, but support needs explicit ACLs and a request/approval workflow for access to escrowed artifacts.

I'll attach a short ops note (Feedback_Escrow_Term_Spec.txt) to the next redline. We should also confirm whether Brightline expects audit logs as part of the evidence package — if so, that'll be another one-off deliverable.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_Brightline_v3.docx (tracked), Brightline_MSA_redline_20280127.pdf (original), Feedback_Escrow_Term_Spec.txt (ops note).

Appreciate the collaboration — happy to hop on a quick call if any of the legal threads need synchronous resolution.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
